citeAs: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe (2025). OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Interspeech 2025.
creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe (Carnegie Mellon University; Honda Research Institute Japan)
description: A cleaned and curated subset of the YODAS (YouTube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech) dataset, produced by applying a scalable data-cleaning pipeline to the raw YODAS data. The pipeline includes CTC-based resegmentation, language-identification (LID) filtering, and CTC-score-based filtering, yielding 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages. This dataset was used to train the OWSM v4 series of open speech foundation models via the ESPnet toolkit.
inLanguage: multilingual (75 languages including en, es, ru, pt, ko, fr, de, it, vi, id and more)
name: espnet_yodas_owsmv4 (Cleaned YODAS for OWSM v4)
rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced: English constitutes the largest share (74.6k hours out of 166k total), while many other languages remain underrepresented. This mirrors the imbalance in the raw YODAS data. The paper explicitly acknowledges this: "Similar to the raw YODAS data, the distribution across languages is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share, whereas many other languages continue to be underrepresented."
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from the raw YODAS (YouTube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech) corpus, which was crawled from the web (YouTube) and contains 370k hours of audio in 149 languages. The raw YODAS data provides unsegmented long-form audio recordings with text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. The cleaned version was produced by applying a three-step pipeline: (1) CTC-based resegmentation to realign audio and text, (2) LID-based filtering to remove utterances with incorrect language labels, and (3) CTC-score-based filtering to remove low-quality audio-text alignments.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw YODAS data: 370k hours of audio in 149 languages, crawled from the web (YouTube). Provided as unsegmented long-form audio recordings, each accompanied by a list of text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. The raw data had not undergone rigorous cleaning and contained annotation errors including mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text.
rai:dataLimitations: The OWSM-CTC v3.2 model used for resegmentation supports only a subset of the languages present in YODAS, limiting coverage. The language distribution is highly imbalanced, with English dominating and many languages underrepresented. The raw YODAS data contains substantial misalignment issues and incorrect language labels that the cleaning pipeline mitigates but may not fully eliminate.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The language distribution across the 75 languages is kept as-is from the raw YODAS data (highly imbalanced, with English constituting the largest share). No resampling or balancing was applied: "For simplicity, in this work, we keep the original distribution without any resampling."
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three-step cleaning pipeline: (1) Resegmentation: audio and text are realigned using the CTC segmentation algorithm with the publicly available OWSM-CTC v3.2 model. Long-form recordings are segmented into shorter utterances of maximum 30 seconds. Utterances consisting exclusively of non-speech elements (e.g., music) are removed. This yields 345k hours across 83 languages. (2) LID-based filtering: text-based LID using fastText and spoken LID using ECAPA-TDNN (SpeechBrain). Only utterances where the original language label matches both the text-predicted and audio-predicted language are retained, yielding 284k hours across 75 languages. (3) CTC-score-based filtering: utterances with low CTC confidence scores are removed using a relative threshold θCTC=0.10 (quantile-based per language). For each long-form utterance, if any constituent short utterance falls in the lowest θCTC quantile, the entire utterance is discarded. Final result: 166k hours across 75 languages.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset advances open academic research by providing a large-scale, publicly released, cleaned multilingual speech dataset under a Creative Commons license. It enables fully open speech foundation models that match or surpass proprietary industrial models, promoting transparency, reproducibility, and accessibility in speech AI research.
rai:dataUseCases: Training multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems; training Whisper-style speech foundation models; multilingual speech processing including language identification (LID) and speech translation (ST).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 model (used for CTC segmentation/resegmentation and confidence scoring); fastText language identification model (text-based LID); ECAPA-TDNN model from SpeechBrain (spoken language identification).
